blocks.text: It is quite the change: a historical archive becoming a podcast. Written text turns into sound and reading into listening. When opening a physical folder in the archive, the yellow-brown fragile pages immediately give their age away. Paper can be touched, smelled.
"Unlike visual information, sound is not something we simply locate outside of ourselves; it literally penetrates our body. It is inside us and all around at the same time." — Tzlil

"Podcasts, more specifically, go hand in hand with productivity: a keyword in our day and age. People, however, also crave to feel closeness. Having something in your ears, a voice accompanying you on your daily commute... it offers the best of both worlds." — Tzlil
This podcast, though, asks more of its listener than most: a binaural space only holds together through headphones, and a listener who moves disturbs the movement of the girl she is following.

"For these reasons, we understood that the podcast we were creating called for a particular form of listening: being attentive, staying still, using headphones, and ideally closing one's eyes. Given that people usually listen to podcasts on the move, this is a lot to ask." — Amit
